body.statement: There is a nonempty relatively open subset \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{abs}}\subset\mathcal G_{\mathrm{loc}}\) of the absorbed region on which \(\|\widetilde D\|_F/\sqrt{NT}\to a_D>0\), \(\widehat\sigma_F\xrightarrow{p}\sigma\), and \(\Pr\{\operatorname{ATT}_{NT}\in\mathrm{CI}_F\}\to0\). Thus coverage is strictly below \(1-\alpha\) on \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{abs}}\), only for bounded \(h=\theta/\sigma\).
body.justification: A selected-factor bias of order \(m^{-1/2}\) dominates the conventional interval width of order \(m^{-1}\).
body.gap: Armstrong, Weidner, and Zeleneev (2026) establish possible weak-factor distortion but not this explicit bounded-local low-rank-treatment zero-coverage region.
body.consumer: The result converts the absorption phase into a formal sensitivity failure for conventional whole-sample Wald inference within the oracle class.
